name: Morphine
summary: The reference full mu-opioid agonist for severe acute and cancer pain, available in multiple routes; its active metabolite M6G accumulates in renal failure.
mechanism: Full agonist at mu-opioid receptors (weaker action at kappa and delta), inhibiting ascending pain transmission and activating descending inhibitory pathways.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic glucuronidation (UGT2B7) to morphine-3-glucuronide (inactive) and morphine-6-glucuronide (M6G, active)

dosing.adult: 2.5–10 mg IV/SC q4h PRN; 10–30 mg PO q4h PRN (IR); extended-release for around-the-clock chronic pain
dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose in renal impairment — M6G accumulates and causes toxicity

safety.pregnancy: Chronic use causes neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome; use near delivery can depress neonatal respiration
warnings: Black box: addiction, abuse, and misuse — risk of opioid use disorder
Black box: life-threatening respiratory depression — especially in opioid-naive patients and with CNS depressants
Black box: accidental ingestion and overdose (especially in children) can be fatal
Black box: neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome with prolonged use during pregnancy
M6G accumulation in renal failure causes sedation, myoclonus, and respiratory depression
Concurrent benzodiazepines or alcohol markedly increase respiratory depression
safety.overdose: Respiratory depression, miosis, coma; naloxone reverses opioid effects (may require repeat doses due to naloxone's short half-life)

indications: Cancer pain and severe chronic pain (extended-release)
clinicalPearls: Oral bioavailability ~30% — use roughly a 3:1 oral-to-IV ratio when converting routes
M6G is active and accumulates in renal failure — new sedation or myoclonus signals metabolite toxicity
good: Severe acute and cancer pain — the reference opioid with multiple routes.
bad: Renal impairment (M6G accumulation), sleep apnea, or when constipation would be dangerous (e.g., postoperative ileus).

provenance.notes: Curated from standard neurology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
